issues.text: The symptom the reader is told to recognise does not happen. Executed in the stage-0 lab box (bash 5.3.9): a CRLF script does not stop — `whoami\r` fails and the next line still runs, exit 0. The name printed is `$'whoami\r'`, the byte spelled out, not "one character longer than the one you typed", so a reader counting characters will not match the screen. And `echo hi\r` gives no error at all: the carriage return sticks to the last word, so the failure needs the command name to be that word. Claim 19 carries the same errors.
issues.quote: stops on a line whose first word it treats as the name of a program to run: the extra byte is glued to that word, so the name it reports is one character longer than the one you typed
issues.fix: Replace the second half with what bash prints: "...reports that it cannot find a program on a line whose first word is also its last: the extra byte is glued to that word, so the name in the message is the one you typed with that byte spelled out on its end, and the lines after it still run." Rewrite claim 19 to its suggested_text, and update quiz q5's stem so it no longer says the script stops.

issues.text: The lesson teaches what depth_notes excludes: "Không đi vào symlink, mount, quyền chi tiết của Linux (chmod bits)". Section 5 names `chmod`, glosses the numeric mode ("`600` asking for reading and writing for the owner and nothing for anyone else") and decodes the mode string into file type plus three rwx triples. The letters half is arguably forced by outline item 2 ("an owner and read/write/execute permissions") and by the script's own output; the numeric mode is not — nothing in the lesson or the quiz needs the reader to know what 600 encodes.
issues.quote: `chmod` changes what a file allows — `600` asking for reading and writing for the owner and nothing for anyone else
issues.fix: Drop the numeric gloss and let the two stat lines carry it: "...and `chmod` changes what a file allows, which is why the second `stat` line differs from the first." Keep the mode-string decoding, which outline item 2 needs. If the owner wants the numeric mode kept, amend depth_notes in content/tracks/foundation/track.yaml first — the lesson may not overrule it by itself.

As written, the sentence hands the reader a fact about the command that their first bare `stat` will contradict, and it sits immediately before the sentence decoding the mode string, so it reads as part of the same explanation.
